name: Baltic Night Discharge
sensor: Sentinel-1 geometry, synthetic pixels (§0 Tier 4, elected)
raster_units: dB (Sigma0 VV), stored as int16 hundredths

raster_method.tier: §0 Tier 4 — synthetic SAR, elected explicitly for SC-01
raster_method.not_a_claim: Scenario imagery for the demo. Not evidence that detection works on real SAR, and no detection metric may be quoted from it (§16).
raster_method.dark_region_geometry: the slick polygon itself — alpha hull of the real 6 h forward drift run — rasterised; no shape is drawn here
raster_method.damping_rationale: midpoint of the 3.0–10.0 dB range CLAUDE.md states for mineral oil against the surrounding sea; deliberately not derived from the scorer's own contrast pivot, which would be circular
raster_method.edge_rationale: one resolution cell — the oil boundary is sharp, so what is modelled is the imaging and multilooking response, not the oil
raster_method.speckle_rationale: IW GRDH ~4.4 looks at 10 m, resampled to 50 m averages 25 pixels
raster_method.background_source: sampled from the drift run's own wind field, so the image and the physics cannot disagree about the sea state
raster_method.wind_law: Sigma0_VV ~ U^1.2 pinned at -10.0 dB for 7.0 m/s at 35.0° — a first-order power law, NOT CMOD
raster_method.range_trend_rationale: ~6 dB across the 250 km IW swath; this is why contrast is measured against a local annulus, not a scene-wide mean

provenance.incidence_angle_deg: authored product geometry, not a measured one
provenance.pixel_spacing_m: authored product geometry, not a measured one
provenance.raster_path: measured from the SC-01 synthetic Sigma0 raster — §0 Tier 4 scenario imagery, not real SAR; no detection metric may be quoted from it (§16)
